# Static-artifact build — decks, reports and microsites

Used at Step 5 when the `static-artifact` lane builds a deck, a report, or a multi-section
microsite, and again whenever one of those is edited after the build. The page-level
build contract lives in [prototype-playbook.md](prototype-playbook.md) (one `.html`, CSS
and JS inline, no build step, no external service); this file adds only what a
slide-shaped artifact needs on top of it. Verification is in
[static-artifact-qa.md](static-artifact-qa.md).

**Boundary.** A deck made of raster slide images generated by an image model belongs to
a slide-image skill such as slide-studio, not to this lane. This lane builds decks in
HTML, where text is text: selectable, searchable, resizable, printable.

## Intake additions for a deck

Fold these into the single Step 1 batch ([ownership-matrix.md](ownership-matrix.md)); do
not open a second round. What is the deck for (pitch, teaching, report-out, talk)? How
long (5–10, 10–20, 20+ slides)? Is the content written, or only ideas? Checking or fixing
an existing HTML deck, whoever built it, does not rerun the seven steps — go straight to
[static-artifact-qa.md](static-artifact-qa.md).

## When the user does not know the taste

Ask one light question instead of asking for a style name: should the deck leave people
impressed, excited, focused, or inspired? Use the answer only to choose which three
deck styles to render — pick them from Partition 2 of
[direction-gate.md](direction-gate.md) — and go to the normal Step 4 gate with real
renders. This is a funnel into the gate, never a catalog of presets: no fixed font and
colour pairings are carried in from anywhere, and every colour still comes through
[color-protocol.md](color-protocol.md). A user who skips the
options is exempt from the gate, as direction-gate already records.

## One slide, one viewport

- Each `.slide` is exactly one viewport: `height: 100vh` followed by `height: 100dvh`,
  `overflow: hidden`. If the content does not fit, **split the slide; never shrink the
  text to fit.**
- Every font size and gap goes through `clamp()`. The floor has no deck exception: body
  text at or above 14px (0.875rem), labels and captions at or above 12px (0.75rem), as in
  the quality floor of `SKILL.md`. If a slide cannot hold at the floor in a short
  landscape viewport, that slide is too full.
- Density **starting points**, not WCAG rules: a title slide holds one heading and one
  line; a content slide 4–6 short bullets or two paragraphs; a grid at most six cards;
  code 8–10 lines; a quote one passage plus attribution; one image per slide, capped
  at a single stated share of the viewport height (pick one number and keep it).
- Short and narrow viewports: add height breakpoints (around 700, 600 and 500px) and a
  width breakpoint (around 600px); on the short ones hide decoration first, then reduce
  gaps, and only then split. These numbers are starting points; the check is the render.
- Scroll-snap needs `scroll-snap-type: y mandatory` on `html` and
  `scroll-snap-align: start` on each slide. Mandatory snapping combined with a wheel
  handler can trap keyboard users: confirm the keys still move through the deck.
- Negated CSS functions fail silently. `-clamp(1rem, 3vw, 2rem)` is dropped by the
  parser and the property is ignored; write `calc(-1 * clamp(1rem, 3vw, 2rem))`.
- `overflow: hidden` hides a violation instead of preventing it, so the build is not
  done until the overflow measurement in the QA file passes.

## Fonts and imagery

Default to a system stack or a face that passed the gate in
[typography-en-vi.md](typography-en-vi.md) (rights, Vietnamese glyphs, loading, fallback).
A font linked from an outside service is allowed only with a fallback stack and is
recorded as a network dependency; there is no rule that system fonts are forbidden.

For images, decide per asset whether to embed or link, as in
[image-sourcing.md](image-sourcing.md). Keep three working rules: never overwrite the
user's original (write a processed copy with a `_processed` suffix); do not repeat an
image on several slides, the logo on the title and closing slides excepted; cap image
height so a picture cannot push text out of the viewport. Several decks in one project
keep their images in `[name]-assets/`; a single deck uses `assets/`, created only when
there are images. Resize with whatever image tool is already on the machine and ask
before installing anything.

## Navigation controls

Required: Arrow keys, PageUp/PageDown, Space, Home and End move between slides; touch
swipe works; a progress indicator shows position; navigation dots are real buttons with
an accessible name such as "Slide 3 of 10" and the current one marked
(`aria-current`). On a slide change, move focus deliberately (the new slide's heading,
with `tabindex="-1"`) and keep the focus indicator visible. If dots are generated by
script and the page DOM is ever saved or re-serialized, empty their container before
regenerating, or every save doubles them.

## Entrance effects

Follow Rule zero in [motion-playbook.md](motion-playbook.md) — content renders whether or
not the animation plays — using its four-part contract and
[motion-patterns.md](motion-patterns.md) MP01 as the recipe: the hidden state is added
by script (a class on the root set by the same script that observes), a failsafe reveals
everything after `load`, reduced motion and a missing observer reveal immediately, and
`@media print` forces the final state. Never write the hidden state into the base
stylesheet. Changing slides by key or swipe is a response to an interaction: it stays
under 300 ms and never delays navigation, and a further key press jumps straight to the
final state. The showcase branch of the playbook applies only to content that appears
inside a slide; staggers still default to the 30–80 ms range and anything longer must be
justified in `06-motion-spec.md`. Atmosphere (background texture, glow, grain) is a
product of the chosen direction, not of a list of effects; tilt, particles and custom
cursors are decorative motion that pass the playbook's gates before they exist.

## Only if you add an edit mode

The default deck has no in-page editing. If a brief asks for one, three traps apply:
a hover-revealed edit toggle built from a CSS sibling selector breaks once the hidden
toggle has `pointer-events: none` — drive it from script with a short delay before it
hides; the export action must strip the editing state before it serializes the page;
and the dot-regeneration trap above. Write no inline-editing code unless the brief asks.

## Converting a PPTX

Keep slide order, speaker notes and the extracted media; then build as a new deck from
that content. No converter ships with this pack. If a script is written, use
`python-pptx` when it is already installed (ask before installing anything), open every
file with `encoding="utf-8"` and write JSON with `ensure_ascii=False`, or Vietnamese text
is saved as escape sequences and mangled by a Windows default code page.

## Exporting a PDF

Two routes, in order of preference:

1. **The browser's own print.** The `@media print` rule from the entrance contract
   already forces final states; add one-slide-per-page breaks. Nothing is installed and
   nothing is served.
2. **A scripted capture.** A `file://` URL needs no server, so open the deck directly.
   If a local server is unavoidable, it must serve only the deck folder and refuse any
   path that leaves it (including encoded dot-dot and slash forms), bind to loopback
   only, use a random port, open the page by the same literal address it bound, and
   delete its temporary files afterwards. Do not run an unpinned `npm install`
   or fetch a browser from the network as part of the export; use a browser already on
   the machine, and report "blocked" when there is none.

## Hand-off

Delete preview and scratch files. Report the absolute path of the file, the number of
slides, the direction chosen, and where the user can safely change content.
